q: In which country are the Callanish (Calanais) Standing Stones located?
n: The Callanish Stones are a Neolithic stone setting on the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides, Scotland.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Neolithic Europe, Callanish

q: In which country are the colossal Olmec Heads found?
n: The Olmec civilization carved these basalt heads on Mexico's Gulf Coast.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Mesoamerica, Olmec

q: Where is the prehistoric site of Göbekli Tepe located?
n: Göbekli Tepe is a Neolithic site in southeastern Turkey and is among the oldest known monumental stone structures.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Neolithic Anatolia, Gobekli Tepe

q: In which country is the megalithic Temple of Tarxien located?
n: The Tarxien Temples are a Neolithic megalithic complex in Tarxien, Malta.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Neolithic Malta, Tarxien

q: On which island are the Bronze Age stone towers known as nuraghe found?
n: Nuraghe are the characteristic Bronze Age stone towers of Sardinia.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Bronze Age Sardinia, nuraghe

q: What is the term for the monumental gateway of an Egyptian temple, formed by two tapering towers flanking the entrance?
n: A pylon is the massive ceremonial gateway of an Egyptian temple. An obelisk is a tapering monolithic shaft, and a mastaba is a flat-roofed tomb.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Ancient Egypt, temple pylon

q: Which church is regarded as the first church built in Constantinople in Byzantine architecture?
n: Hagia Irene, first raised under Constantine I, is held to be the first church of Constantinople. It was rebuilt under Justinian. Hagia Sophia is the larger and later church beside it.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Byzantine, churches of Constantinople

q: Which Byzantine constructional device permits a circular dome to be placed over a square room?
n: A pendentive is a spherical triangle that carries the dome's load down to the corners of the square base, as in Hagia Sophia.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Byzantine, pendentives and domes

q: Which description best fits the interior of a Gothic cathedral?
o: Light and airy, thanks to tall stained-glass windows
Dark and massive, with thick walls and small windows
Domed and covered in gold mosaics
Low and horizontal, with timber-truss roofs
n: Gothic structure (ribbed vaults, pointed arches, flying buttresses) frees the walls for large stained-glass windows. The dark massive interior describes Romanesque.
ref: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order, 4th ed. - Light and structure; Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Gothic

q: Which pair of features is characteristic of Gothic architecture?
n: Flying buttresses carry the vault thrust outward, which allows tall walls with pointed arches.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Gothic, ribbed vault and flying buttress

q: St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City is an example of which architectural style?
n: St. Peter's Basilica is the principal example of Renaissance church architecture, with Bramante, Michelangelo and later Maderno among its architects.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Italian Renaissance, St. Peter's Basilica

q: Pisa Cathedral is an example of which architectural style?
n: Pisa Cathedral is a masterpiece of Pisan Romanesque, with tiers of blind arcades on its facade.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Pisan Romanesque

q: The Cathedral of Santiago de Compostela, seen from its Obradoiro facade, is an example of which style?
n: The Obradoiro facade is a Baroque work of 1738-1750 by Fernando de Casas Novoa. The cathedral behind it keeps its Romanesque core.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Spanish Baroque, Obradoiro facade

q: The Virginia State Capitol, designed by Thomas Jefferson after the Maison Carrée, is an example of which style?
n: The Virginia State Capitol is a Roman-temple-form building modeled by Jefferson on the Maison Carree at Nimes, so the style is Classical (Roman Revival).
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - American Neoclassicism, Jefferson

q: Milan Cathedral (Duomo di Milano) is an example of which architectural style?
n: Milan Cathedral is a large late-Gothic cathedral, noted for its forest of pinnacles and spires.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Italian Gothic, Milan Cathedral

q: Who is the latest National Artist for Architecture in the Philippines?
n: Proclamation No. 1414, signed September 1, 2026, named Gabriel "Gabby" Formoso National Artist for Architecture, posthumously, the seventh in the field. Older reviewers still give Manosa, who was proclaimed in 2018.
ref: Proclamation No. 1414 (September 1, 2026); NCCA, Order of National Artists for Architecture

q: Who is known as the "Dean of Philippine Architecture"?
n: Juan Nakpil, the first National Artist for Architecture (1973), is commonly called the Dean of Philippine Architecture.
ref: NCCA, Order of National Artists for Architecture; Juan F. Nakpil (1973)

q: Which Filipino architect, artist and interior designer is known for his use of concrete, floating volumes and simple design?
n: Leandro Locsin, National Artist for Architecture (1990), is known for the "floating volume" of the Cultural Center of the Philippines.
ref: NCCA, Order of National Artists for Architecture; Leandro V. Locsin (1990)

q: Who designed the Tate Modern in London?
n: Herzog & de Meuron converted the Bankside Power Station into Tate Modern.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris?
n: Frank Gehry designed the glass-sail building in the Bois de Boulogne.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Imperial War Museum North in Manchester?
n: Libeskind's design uses three interlocking shards representing a shattered globe.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Centre Pompidou-Metz?
n: Shigeru Ban designed the Metz branch with Jean de Gastines. The Paris Centre Pompidou is by Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers, which is the common trap.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed Finlandia Hall in Helsinki?
n: Finlandia Hall is one of Alvar Aalto's late major works.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Nordic modernism, Alvar Aalto

q: Who designed Washington Dulles International Airport?
n: Eero Saarinen designed the Dulles terminal with its sweeping suspended roof.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - mid-century modernism, Eero Saarinen

q: Who designed the Wainwright Building in St. Louis?
n: The Wainwright Building (Adler & Sullivan) is an early steel-frame skyscraper by Louis Sullivan.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Chicago School, Adler and Sullivan

q: Who designed the Zentrum Paul Klee in Bern?
n: Renzo Piano designed the three-wave Paul Klee Center.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: The Hundertwasserhaus in Vienna is credited to which artist-architect?
n: Friedensreich Hundertwasser is the credited designer. The architect Josef Krawina was his collaborator, a name often misspelled as 'Joseph Krawin'.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture, Vienna

q: Who designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
n: Gaudí took over the project in 1883 and devoted the rest of his career to it.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Catalan Modernisme, Antoni Gaudi
